                                       21                                    NATURE OF THE ACTION
                                       22          1.      This action arises under the Declaratory Judgment Act, 28 U.S.C. §§ 2201 and 2022.

                                       23   New Era seeks a declaration that no valid or enforceable arbitration agreement was formed between

                                       24   New Era and Defendants, and that New Era cannot be forced to participate in any arbitration

                                       25   proceeding, including the pending one-hundred individual arbitrations arising primarily under the
                                       26   California Invasion of Privacy Act (“CIPA”) filed by Defendants with the American Arbitration

                                       27   Association (“AAA”) (the “CIPA Arbitrations”).

                                       28          2.      Beginning on or about March 26, 2026, Defendants—acting through their counsel

                                                                                   1

                                        1   Bryson Harris Suciu Demay PLLC—filed one hundred arbitrations against New Era with the AAA

                                        2   (Case No. 01-26-0001-6664). See Exhibit A (March 26, 2026, Representative AAA Demand

                                        3   Letter); Exhibit B (April 8, 2026, AAA CIPA Arbitrations Confirmation Letter); Exhibit C
                                        4   (Affirmation of Hunter Bryson).

                                        5            3.     In the demands filed with AAA, Defendants invoke an arbitration clause contained

                                        6   in New Era’s online Terms and Conditions (“Terms”),1 but allege no facts sufficient to show that

                                        7   an enforceable agreement was formed.           They allege that they visited Plaintiff’s website at
                                        8   www.neweracap.com (the “Site”) on an unspecified occasion and that information concerning their

                                        9   visit was shared with one or more third-party marketing partners. They do not allege how or when

                                       10   a contract was formed, whether they offered any consideration for any such contract, whether there
THREE EMBARCADERO CENTER, 7TH FLOOR




                                       11   was a meeting of the minds as to contract formation, or how they manifested assent to the Terms.
SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA 94111-4070
  BRYAN CAVE LEIGHTON PAISNER LLP




                                       12   No valid and enforceable agreement to arbitrate was ever formed between New Era and Defendants.

                                       13            4.     It is black letter law that arbitration is a matter of contract and that a party cannot be

                                       14   compelled to arbitrate unless a valid and enforceable agreement to arbitrate exists. Chabolla v.
                                       15   ClassPass Inc., 129 F.4th 1147, 1153–1154 (9th Cir. 2025) (“[T]o hold Chabolla to an arbitration

                                       16   clause we must discern whether she entered into such a contract in the first place.”); Berman v.

                                       17   Freedom Fin. Network, LLC, 30 F.4th 849, 855 (9th Cir. 2022) (“The [FAA] requires district courts
                                       18   to compel arbitration of claims covered by an enforceable arbitration agreement.” (emphasis

                                       19   added)).

                                       20            5.     An actual and justiciable controversy currently exists between the parties.

                                       21   Defendants have already filed the CIPA Arbitrations with AAA, those proceedings are pending,
                                       22   and New Era has been forced to pay thousands of dollars in arbitration fees to avoid waiver and

                                       23   preserve its rights. See Exhibits A, B. New Era brings this action to establish what Defendants

                                       24   deny: that no valid arbitration agreement exists, New Era cannot be forced to arbitrate Defendants’

                                       25   claims, AAA lacks jurisdiction over the CIPA Arbitrations, and the CIPA Arbitrations must
                                       26   therefore be dismissed.

                                       17           135.    To determine whether the parties have an agreement to arbitrate, state-law contract
                                       18   formation principles apply. Berman, 30 F.4th at 855. California contract law therefore applies.

                                       19           136.    Under California law, an online contract requires “actual or constructive notice of

                                       20   the agreement and the parties must manifest mutual assent.” Keebaugh, 100 F.4th at 1013–14

                                       21   (citation omitted); see also Cal. Civ. Code §§ 1580–1585 (stating that acceptance must be “absolute
                                       22   and unqualified,” before any binding agreement can exist). Assent may be manifested through

                                       23   conduct, but “[t]he conduct of a party is not effective as a manifestation of his assent unless he

                                       24   intends to engage in the conduct and knows or has reason to know that the other party may infer

                                       25   from his conduct that he assents.” Keebaugh, 100 F.4th at 1014 (quoting Berman, 30 F.4th at 855).
                                       26           137.    In California, online contracts are categorized “by the way in which the user

                                       27   purportedly gives their assent to be bound by the associated terms: browsewraps, clickwraps,

                                       28   scrollwraps, and sign-in wraps.” Id. (quoting Sellers v. JustAnswer LLC, 289 Cal. Rptr. 3d 1, 15

                                       17           135.    To determine whether the parties have an agreement to arbitrate, state-law contract

                                       18   formation principles apply. Berman, 30 F.4th at 855. California contract law therefore applies.

                                       19           136.    Under California law, an online contract requires “actual or constructive notice of

                                       20   the agreement and the parties must manifest mutual assent.” Keebaugh, 100 F.4th at 1013–14

                                       21   (citation omitted); see also Cal. Civ. Code §§ 1580–1585 (stating that acceptance must be “absolute

                                       22   and unqualified,” before any binding agreement can exist). Assent may be manifested through

                                       23   conduct, but “[t]he conduct of a party is not effective as a manifestation of his assent unless he

                                       24   intends to engage in the conduct and knows or has reason to know that the other party may infer

                                       25   from his conduct that he assents.” Keebaugh, 100 F.4th at 1014 (quoting Berman, 30 F.4th at 855).

                                       26           137.    In California, online contracts are categorized “by the way in which the user

                                       27   purportedly gives their assent to be bound by the associated terms: browsewraps, clickwraps,

                                       28   scrollwraps, and sign-in wraps.” Id. (quoting Sellers v. JustAnswer LLC, 289 Cal. Rptr. 3d 1, 15

                                        3   of use merely by browsing the site.” Id. (quoting Sellers, 289 Cal. Rptr. 3d at 15). The “website’s

                                        4   terms and conditions of use are generally posted on the website via a hyperlink at the bottom of the

                                        5   screen.” Nguyen v. Barnes & Noble Inc., 763 F.3d 1171, 1176 (9th Cir. 2014).

                                        6          139.    A clickwrap agreement is where “website users are required to click on an ‘I agree’

                                        7   box after being presented with a list of terms and conditions of use.” Id. at 1175–76; see also

                                        8   Chabolla, 129 F.4th at 1154 (“Courts routinely enforce clickwraps.”).

                                        9          140.    A scrollwrap agreement, which provides the strongest notice, is “where the user

                                       10   must scroll through all the Terms of Service before they can click the mandatory ‘I agree’ box.”

                                       11   Keebaugh, 100 F.4th at 1014; Chabolla, 129 F.4th at 1154 (noting scrollwraps are “usually
